profile_text.body:
Cerence Inc. is a public company, traded under the ticker CRNC and headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts, with CIK 0001768267. Its site describes it as delivering conversational and agentic AI-powered user experiences for automotive and beyond, built on CaLLM, which the company describes as its family of language models. The site says the company is moving to advance generative AI and LLM-powered innovation that it believes will be central to the automotive and transportation user experience, and that it offers tailor-made AI solutions integrated with vehicle makers' own brand identities.

Among the products described on the site is Cerence Emergency Vehicle Detection, or EVD, which the company says is already deployed in production vehicles. According to the site, EVD uses vehicle microphones and AI trained to distinguish sirens from traffic, road noise, music and other sounds, and can detect and localize more than 1,500 emergency sirens across nearly 50 countries, identifying approaching emergency vehicles from more than 300 meters away with interior microphones and beyond 800 meters with exterior microphones. The site also describes dynamic speech enhancement for multi-seat in-car environments, demonstrated by Timo Matheja and Stefan Hamerich, which lets passengers in different zones make requests at the same time. A site article on Zero Trust Architecture for in-car assistants is credited to Kaivan Karimi of Cerence AI and Frank Kaleck of Microsoft. The company reported third quarter results with revenue up 12% YoY, connected services revenue up 20% YoY, and operating cash flow of $20M supporting a first-ever share repurchase program.

The company's recorded legal exposure is in Massachusetts, with a count of 187.
